description: What was learned on a product-scoping call. Every field is optional on purpose: an absent field means the call did not cover it, which is information. Never infer a value that was not said.

business.description: How the company actually operates today.

size.description: Headcount, crews, or however they described their scale, in their terms.

concurrent_projects.description: How many jobs run at once, as stated. Keep their exact number or range.

project_shape.description: Typical duration, value, and how a job progresses from won to finished.

who_they_work_with.description: Subcontractors, employees, engineers, architects, clients — and which of those they need visibility into.

today.description: The current way of working. Mechanics, not summaries — this is the baseline any new tool has to beat.

tools_in_use.description: Spreadsheets, paper, whiteboard, WhatsApp, accounting software, anything named.

how_status_is_tracked.description: How they find out where a project stands right now.

what_breaks.description: Specific failures they described, ideally with the story attached.

cost_of_the_problem.description: Money, time, or lost work they attributed to the current way. Only if quantified or clearly implied.

previously_tried.description: Tools or processes attempted before and abandoned, and why. Absence of an answer here is itself worth knowing.

users.description: Every distinct kind of person who would touch the system. Field users matter most: a tool the office likes and the crews refuse to open has failed.

tech_comfort.description: How they described this person's relationship with technology.

adoption_risk.description: Any reason given to think this group would resist using it.

needs.description: Capabilities discussed, each ranked as the client ranked it — not as the agent judged it.

why.description: The underlying problem it solves, in their words.

evidence.description: The concrete situation they described that makes this real.

profitability.description: Called out separately because it was the stated reason for the project.

what_they_would_need.description: The inputs required to know whether a job is profitable.

definition_of_profitable.description: How they actually calculate it, if they said.

offline_required.description: Whether sites have connectivity, and what must work without it.

integrations.description: Systems this must exchange data with — accounting, payroll, anything named.

compliance_or_reporting.description: Anything they are obliged to produce for clients, engineers, or regulators.

existing_data.description: What would have to be migrated in.

who_decides.description: Anyone besides the person on the call who has a say.

timeline_pressure.description: Any date driving this, and what makes it a date.

budget_signal.description: Only what they volunteered. The agent must not have raised price.

what_success_looks_like.description: How they would judge, in a year, that this was worth doing.

call_quality.description: How much to trust the rest of this record.

topics_not_covered.description: Agenda items the call never reached.

unresolved_questions.description: Things asked but not really answered, or answered vaguely.

client_energy.description: Engaged, rushed, distracted, sceptical — anything that colours the answers.

follow_ups.description: Anything the client said they would send or check.

notable_quotes.description: Their own words where the phrasing carries meaning a paraphrase would lose.
